the magnetic properties of IMAGES MD01–2401 are not reliable for high-resolution paleoenvironmental studies in the Japan Sea.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
magnetic properties of the Japan Sea sediments are strongly affected by the early diagenetic process of the sediments.

the TL layers in the IMAGES MD01–2406 record a rapid increase in the concentration of ferromagnetic minerals in the Japan Sea, probably due to the deposition of a large volume of organic matter and/or the supply of Fe-rich minerals from the continent.

the diagenetic modification of the magnetic properties in the Japan Sea sediments is more complicated than those in the Mediterranean Sea, because the Japan Sea sedimants contain more variable lithology including volcanic ashes and are affected by more complex diagenetic processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

diagenetic changes are likely to affect the magnetic properties of sediments in the Japan Sea, and that the magnetic properties of TL dark layers should be treated with caution when used as a paleoenvironmental proxy.

the diagenetic alteration of magnetic minerals in the hemipelagic sedments of the Japan Sea is more complicated than that of the Mediterranean Sea, because of the difference in depositional environments.
diagenetic changes in magnetic properties of sediments must be carefully taken into account for paleoenvironmental studies.
